rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazakkā means purifying oneself from associating partners with God and from sins.
rows.anchor: تطهر من الشرك والمعاصي .   أو تطهر للصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the person purifies himself for prayer.
rows.anchor: أو تطهر للصلاة .   أو تكثر من التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can also mean increasing in piety, from zakā meaning growth.
rows.anchor: أو تكثر من التقوى ،   من الزكاة وهو النماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means performing zakāh, just as tasaddaqa means giving charity.
rows.anchor: أو تفعل من الزكاة ،   كتصدق من الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has thirty verses; another count gives twenty-nine.
rows.anchor: مكية وآياتها 30 وقيل : 29

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by dawn, as in the oaths by daybreak and by morning's breathing in other sūras.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالفجر كما أقسم بالصبح في قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation takes al-fajr as the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: [ التكوير : 18 ] ،   وقيل : بصلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage connects to the Lord keeping watch: God seeks human obedience and preparation for the afterlife and watches for the disobedient with punishment, while people pursue immediate pleasures.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يريد من الإنسان إلا الطاعة والسعي للعاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses balance through an implicit subject in the second: the first man's predicate is “he says,” while the intervening time phrase is delayed; the second “he says” likewise needs an understood subject.
rows.anchor: هما متوازنان من حيث إن التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both wealth's expansion and its restriction test the servant: abundance tests gratitude rather than ingratitude, and constraint tests patience rather than dismay; their wisdom is the same.
rows.anchor: لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling abundance honor is proper because it is a freely bestowed favor; restricted provision is not humiliation, since withholding a favor is not an insult, and a patron may neither honor nor humiliate.
rows.anchor: وأما التقدير فليس بإهانة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that the rebuke targets claiming wealth was deserved because of one's status or ancestry; God grants it freely, and regards piety rather than lineage and pedigree as worthy of honor.
rows.anchor: إنما أنكر قوله ربي أكرمن وذمه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer carries the rebuke over to “my Lord humiliated me”: people acknowledge God's generosity when favored but wrongly call the absence of a favor humiliation.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن ينساق الإنكار والذمّ إلى قوله : { رَبّى أَهَانَنِ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported readings have qaddara with a light or doubled dāl; at pause, akraman and ahānan have a still nūn for readers who omit the yāʾ in continuation, relying on its kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «فقدر » بالتخفيف والتشديد وأكرمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the human's claim and introduces conduct worse than that claim.
rows.anchor: كَلاَّ } ردع للإنسان عن قوله : ثم قال : بل هناك شر من القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God grants abundant wealth, they fail to fulfill its obligation by attending to the orphan and treating the orphan kindly.
rows.anchor: فلا يؤدون ما يلزمهم فيه من إكرام اليتيم بالتفقد والمبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not urge their households to feed the poor, and consume wealth like cattle.
rows.anchor: وحض أهله على طعام المسكين ويأكلونه أكل الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their conduct also includes loving wealth, hoarding it, and withholding its due rights.
rows.anchor: ويأكلونه أكل الأنعام ،   ويحبونه فيشحون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs here and what follows are read in either third person, “they,” or second person, “you.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء «يكرمون » وما بعده بالياء والتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥāḍḍūn means that you urge one another; Ibn Masʿūd's reading has the tāʾ vowelled with ḍamma, from muḥāḍḍa.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «تحاضون » أي : يحض بعضكم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jammā means abundant and intense love, accompanied by greed and avarice and by withholding people's rights.
rows.anchor: كثيرا شديدا مع الحرص والشره ومنع الحقوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By implication, God says this to the believer, either addressing the person directly in honor as He addressed Moses, or speaking through an angel.
rows.anchor: إما أن يكلمه إكراما له كما كلم موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tranquil soul is secure, undisturbed by fear or grief; it is the believing soul, or one settled in truth with certainty untroubled by doubt.
rows.anchor: الآمنة التي لا يستفزها خوف ولا حزن

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's reading adds “secure,” supporting the explanation that the soul is safe from fear and grief.
rows.anchor: قراءة أبي بن كعب : «يا أيتها النفس الآمنة المطمئنة »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may come at death, at resurrection, or upon entry into Paradise.
rows.anchor: إما عند الموت .   وإما عند البعث ،   وإما عند دخول الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return to your Lord's appointed meeting, content with what you have received and accepted by God.
rows.anchor: على معنى : ارجعي إلى موعد ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enter among God's righteous servants and join their ranks.
rows.anchor: في جملة عبادي الصالحين ،   وانتظمي في سلكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spender boasts of the large wealth spent on what pre-Islamic people called generosity and styled as lofty deeds and objects of pride.
rows.anchor: يريد كثرة ما أنفقه فيما كان أهل الجاهلية يسمونها مكارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While he spent to be seen and to boast, God saw him and kept watch over him.
rows.anchor: حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رئاء الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another contextual reading takes the address in the town oath as referring to Muhammad: his dwelling there, free of its inhabitants' sins, is part of the town's honor and grounds for the oath.
rows.anchor: ومن شرفه أنك حل به مما يقترفه أهله من المآثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, “in hardship” means illness: a diseased heart and corrupt inward state, describing those God knew would not believe or do righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: أي : في مرض : وهو مرض القلب وفساد الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the person who thinks no one can overcome him as Abū al-Ashadd, a strong man who challenged others to remove him from a stretched hide and left only his footprints.
rows.anchor: هو أبو الأشد ، وكان قويا يبسط له الأديم العكاظي فيقوم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies him as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الوليد بن المغيرة «لبدا » قرىء بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lubadan is read with ḍamma or kasra as a plural of lubda, a felted heap; other readings are lubudan, plural of lubūd, and lubbadan, plural of lābid.
rows.anchor: جمع لبدة ولبدة ،   وهو ما تلبد يريد الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave the human two eyes with which to see visible things.
rows.anchor: يبصر بهما المرئيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ is instrumental or causal, as in “I wrote with a pen”; ṭaghwā derives from ṭughyān, with the noun's yāʾ shifted to wāw unlike the adjective.
rows.anchor: مثلها في : كتبت بالقلم .   والطغوى من الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The main explanation is that Thamūd committed denial because of its transgression, as one might say someone wronged another through daring against God.
rows.anchor: مثلها في : كتبت بالقلم .   والطغوى من الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Thamūd denied the punishment threatened against it, a punishment described as overwhelming.
rows.anchor: كذبت بما أوعدت به من عذابها ذي الطغوى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan read biṭughwāhā with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, like the verbal nouns al-ḥusnā and al-rujʿā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : «بطغواها » بضم الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has twenty-one verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وآياتها إحدى وعشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thing the night covers may be the sun, as in the oath by night when it covers it.
rows.anchor: إما الشمس من قوله : { واليل إِذَا يغشاها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may be the daytime, as in the statement that night covers day.
rows.anchor: وإما النهار من قوله : { يغشي الليل النهار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covered object may instead be anything that darkness conceals.
rows.anchor: وإما كل شيء يواريه بظلامه من قوله : { إذا وقب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may disdain what is with God as though he does not need it, and so fail to fear God.
rows.anchor: وزهد فيما عند الله كأنه مستغن عنه فلم يتقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Or he treats worldly desires as sufficient in place of Paradise's delights, the contrast to “he was God-fearing.”
rows.anchor: عن نعيم الجنة ،   لأنه في مقابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God abandons him and withholds grace until obedience becomes his hardest and most difficult task.
rows.anchor: ونمنعه الألطاف ،   حتى تكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه وأشده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The easy path is named for the ease of its outcome, while the hard path is named for its difficult outcome.
rows.anchor: طريقة الخير باليسرى ،   لأن عاقبتها اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God will guide them in the afterlife to the two paths, Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: أو أراد بهما طريقي الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says these verses were revealed concerning Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb.
rows.anchor: نزلتا في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “what will avail him?” functions as a denial that anything can benefit him.
rows.anchor: استفهام في معنى الإنكار .   أو نفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taraddā is derived from radā, to perish, and here means death.
rows.anchor: تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك ،   يريد : الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means falling into the grave after burial.
rows.anchor: أو تردى في الحفرة إذا قبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is falling into the depths of Hell.
rows.anchor: أو تردى في قعر جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording answers the objection that all wicked people enter Hell and all righteous people avoid it: the passage contrasts a leading disbeliever with a leading believer and hyperbolically singles each out as if Hell or Paradise were made just for him.
rows.anchor: الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most God-fearing person is hyperbolically singled out for salvation, as though Paradise were created only for him.
rows.anchor: وجعل مختصا بالنجاة ،   كأن الجنة لم تخلق إلا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the most wretched as Abū Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf, and the most God-fearing as Abū Bakr.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From zakāʾ, it means seeking to be pure in God's sight, without seeking ostentation or reputation.
rows.anchor: أي : يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the verb form meaning to give zakāh.
rows.anchor: أو يتفعل من الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatazakkā can be an appositive within the relative clause and then has no syntactic position, or a circumstantial accusative describing the subject of yuʾtī.
rows.anchor: إن جعلته بدلا من { يؤتي } فلا محل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening enumerates God's favors from the Prophet's earliest upbringing, encouraging him to expect further favor and honor without losing patience or becoming distressed.
rows.anchor: عدّد عليه نعمه وأياديه ،   وأنه لم يخله منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajada here means “know”; both following nouns are its objects, so the sense is “were you not an orphan?”
rows.anchor: من الوجود الذي بمعنى العلم : والمنصوبان مفعولا وجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's father died while he was a six-month fetus, his mother died when he was eight, and his uncle Abū Ṭālib cared for him and raised him well by God's kindness.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أباه مات وهو جنين قد أتت عليه ستة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhsharī rejects as an inventive interpretation taking yatīm like “a unique pearl,” meaning the Prophet was peerless among Quraysh.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير : أنه من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading fa-āwā can mean he sheltered you, from āwā meaning āwāhu, or that he showed you mercy; a shepherd's usage attests the first verb.
rows.anchor: وهو على معنيين : إما من أواه بمعنى آواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍāllan means lacking knowledge of revealed religious law and matters learned through transmission, as in the verse “you did not know the Book.”
rows.anchor: معناه الضلال عن علم الشرائع وما طريقه السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says he was lost as a child in a ravine near Mecca and Abū Jahl returned him to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ضل في صباه في بعض شعاب مكة ، فردّه أبو جهل إلى عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Ḥalīma lost him at Mecca's gate after weaning him and bringing him back to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أضلته حليمة عند باب مكة حين فطمته وجاءت به لتردّه على عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account says he lost his way on the Syria journey with Abū Ṭālib.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ضلّ في طريق الشام حين خرج به أبو طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided him by teaching him the Qurʾān and religious laws, or by removing him from the error of his grandfather and uncle.
rows.anchor: فهداك : فعرفك القرآن والشرائع .   أو فأزال ضلالك عن جدك وعمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If being with his people for forty years means lacking revealed knowledge, that is acceptable; if it means sharing their religion and unbelief, it is impossible, since prophets are protected from blameworthy sins before and after prophecy.
rows.anchor: فإن أراد أنه كان على خلوّهم عن العلوم السمعية ،   فنعم ؛ وإن أراد أنه كان على دينهم وكفرهم ،   فمعاذ الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀʾilan means poor or destitute.
rows.anchor: { عَآئِلاً } فقيراً .   وقرىء : «عيلاً » كما قرىء : سيحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has ʿayilan, with a morphological comparison to sayiḥāt.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «عيلاً » كما قرىء : سيحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enriched him through Khadīja's wealth, or through the spoils granted to him.
rows.anchor: فأغناك بمال خديجة .   أو بما أفاء عليك من الغنائم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that his provision was placed beneath the shade of his spear.
rows.anchor: جعل رزقي تحت ظل رمحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God made him content and enriched his heart.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قنعك وأغنى قلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has nineteen verses.
rows.anchor: مكية ،   وآياتها تسع عشرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid say this was the first sūra revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد : هي أول سورة نزلت

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators hold that al-Fātiḥa was revealed first, followed by Sūrat al-Qalam.
rows.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن الفاتحة أول ما نزل ثم سورة القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-smi rabbika is an accusative circumstantial phrase: read beginning with the name of your Lord, saying “In the name of God,” then read.
rows.anchor: النصب على الحال ،   أي : اقرأ مفتتحاً باسم ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis leaves khalaqa without an understood object: God alone brought creation into being and there is no other creator.
rows.anchor: إما أن لا يقدر له مفعول وأن يراد أنه الذي حصل منه الخلق واستأثر به لا خالق سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, its unexpressed object is “everything”: the word is unrestricted, so no subset of created things is more deserving of being supplied.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يقدر ويراد خلق كل شيء ،   فيتناول كل مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching people what they did not know shows God's complete generosity and moves them from the darkness of ignorance to the light of knowledge.
rows.anchor: فدلّ على كمال كرمه بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا ،   ونقلهم من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing has immense benefits: it records knowledge and wisdom, preserves earlier peoples' accounts and sayings and the revealed books, and sustains religious and worldly affairs.
rows.anchor: ونبه على فضل علم الكتابة لما فيه من المنافع العظيمة التي لا يحيط بها إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen and script alone suffice as evidence of God's subtle wisdom and fine ordering.
rows.anchor: ولو لم يكن على دقيق حكمة الله ولطيف تدبيره ودليل إلا أمر القلم والخط ،   لكفى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's couplets picture the writing instruments as black-legged figures whose motion begins when white blades play upon them, praising the pen's work.
rows.anchor: ولبعضهم في صفة القلم : وَرَوَاقِمُ رُقْشٍ كَمِثْلِ أَرَاقِم

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr read, “He taught writing with the pen.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير : «علم الخط بالقلم »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching people what they did not know shows God's complete generosity and moves them from the darkness of ignorance to the light of knowledge.
rows.anchor: فدلّ على كمال كرمه بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا ،   ونقلهم من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing preserves sciences, wisdom, earlier peoples' reports and sayings, and revealed books; without it, religion and worldly affairs could not be properly sustained.
rows.anchor: وما دوّنت العلوم ،   ولا قيدت الحكم ،   ولا ضبطت أخبار الأولين ومقالاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen and script are by themselves enough to demonstrate God's precise wisdom and subtle governance.
rows.anchor: ولو لم يكن على دقيق حكمة الله ولطيف تدبيره ودليل إلا أمر القلم والخط ،   لكفى به

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr's reading specifies that God taught writing with the pen.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير : «علم الخط بالقلم »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the person who responds to God's favor with transgression, though that unbelief is left implicit in the context.
rows.anchor: ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه ،   وإن لم يذكر لدلالة الكلام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has three verses.
rows.anchor: مكية ،   وآياتها ثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God swears by the ʿAṣr prayer because of its merit; the “middle prayer” in Ḥafṣa's codex is identified as ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: أقسم بصلاة العصر لفضلها ،   بدليل قوله تعالى : ( والصلاة الوسطى )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that missing the ʿAṣr prayer is like losing one's family and wealth.
rows.anchor: وقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : « من فاتته العصر فكأنما وتر أهله وماله »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ʿAṣr prayer is especially demanding because people are absorbed in trade and livelihood late in the day.
rows.anchor: ولأن التكليف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجاراتهم ومكاسبهم آخر النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-ʿaṣr means evening, like the morning oath, since both times show signs of God's power.
rows.anchor: أو أقسم بالعشي كما أقسم بالضحى لما فيهما جميعا من دلائل القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead mean time, whose passing contains many kinds of marvels.
rows.anchor: أو أقسم بالزمان لما في مروره من أصناف العجائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan, though it is also said to be Medinan; it has seven verses.
rows.anchor: مكية ،   وقيل : مدنية ،   وآياتها سبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading arayta deletes the hamza; it is not preferred because deletion belongs to the imperfect and Arabic usage does not attest rīt, though initial interrogation makes it easier; a cited line supplies rayta.
rows.anchor: قرىء : «أريت » ،   بحذف الهمزة ،   وليس بالاختيار

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read arāytaka, adding the second-person suffix, as in the address in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «أرأيتك » بزيادة حرف الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: do you know who the denier of recompense is, if you do not already know?
rows.anchor: والمعنى : هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier of recompense drives the orphan away roughly and harmfully, rejecting the child with harsh rebuke.
rows.anchor: هو الذي { يَدُعُّ اليتيم } أي : يدفعه دفعا عنيفا بجفوة وأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading without gemination, yadaʿ, means leaving and neglecting.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «يدع » أي : يترك ويجفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding warning powerfully shows that sin signals weak faith and loose certainty; the text then adds a warning of woe for those who pray.
rows.anchor: وما أبلغه في التحذير من المعصية ،   وأنها جديرة بأن يستدل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They neglect prayer through indifference, letting it lapse or delaying it beyond its time.
rows.anchor: الذين يسهون عن الصلاة قلة مبالاة بها ،   حتى تفوتهم أو يخرج وقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may also rush prayer instead of following the Prophet and the early generations, lacking humility and ignoring disliked acts such as fidgeting, yawning, and looking around.
rows.anchor: أو لا يصلونها كما صلاها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والسلف ،   ولكن ينقرونها نقراً من غير خشوع وإخبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include playing with beard or clothes, excessive yawning, looking around, and not knowing how many units they finished or what they recited, as with many ostentatious worshippers.
rows.anchor: من العبث باللحية ،   والثياب ،   وكثرة التثاؤب ،   والالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their neglect of prayer, the pillar distinguishing faith from unbelief, their ostentation, a branch of associating partners, and withholding zakāh, prayer's counterpart, expose them as deniers of judgment; even some scholars display this trait.
rows.anchor: التي هي عماد الدين ،   والفارق بين الإيمان والكفر والرياء الذي هو شعبة من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another syntax coordinates fa-dhālika with the denier, as a noun or description; the answer to “Have you seen?” is omitted and indicated by what follows, and the plural denotes the generic singular.
rows.anchor: وطريقة أخرى : أن يكون { فَذَلِكَ } عطفاً على { الذي يُكَذّبُ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAn ṣalātihim means neglecting or turning away from prayer, characteristic of hypocrites or shameless sinners; fī ṣalātihim would mean distraction within prayer, which afflicts any Muslim, even the Prophet, and occasions prostration for forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: أنهم ساهون عنها سهو ترك لها

rows.speaker: أنس رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Anas praised God that the wording says “about their prayer” rather than “in their prayer.”
rows.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه : الحمد لله على أن لم يقل في صلاتهم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read lāhūn, “heedless.”
rows.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه : الحمد لله على أن لم يقل في صلاتهم .   وقرأ ابن مسعود : «لاهون »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Murāʾāh is a reciprocal form of showing: the ostentatious worshipper displays his deed to people, seeking their praise and admiration.
rows.anchor: هي مفاعلة من الإراءة ؛ لأن المرائي يري الناس عمله ،   وهم يرونه الثناء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obligatory good works should be done publicly as Islamic emblems, removing suspicion because neglecting them merits blame; voluntary acts are better concealed unless shown to encourage emulation.
rows.anchor: فمن حق الفرائض الإعلان بها وتشهيرها ،   لقوله عليه الصلاة السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Showing an act is ostentation only when the aim is to be seen and praised for piety; displaying it to encourage others is good.
rows.anchor: فإن أظهره قاصداً للاقتداء به كان جميلاً ،   وإنما الرياء أن يقصد بالإظهار أن تراه الأعين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Someone saw a man prolonging a prostration of gratitude in the mosque and remarked that it would be better if done at home, suspecting ostentation and reputation-seeking.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم : أنه رأى رجلاً في المسجد قد سجد سجدة الشكر وأطالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding ostentation is difficult except for people disciplined in sincerity.
rows.anchor: على أن اجتناب الرياء صعب إلا على المرتاضين بالإخلاص

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said ostentation is more hidden than a black ant crawling on black cloth in a dark night.
rows.anchor: الرياء أخفى من دبيب النملة السوداء في الليلة المظلمة على المسح الأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-māʿūn means zakāh; the poet al-Rāʿī uses the word of people withholding their customary contribution.
rows.anchor: قال الراعي : قَوْمٌ عَلَى الإسْلاَمِ لما يَمْنَعُوا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says al-māʿūn is what people customarily lend one another, such as an axe, pot, bucket, or fire striker.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود : ما يتعاور في العادة من الفأس والقدر

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha says it means water, fire, and salt.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة : الماء والنار والملح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Refusing these items can be forbidden by religious law when they are requested from necessity, and is poor conduct even without necessity.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون منع هذه الأشياء محظورا في الشريعة إذا استعيرت عن اضطرار ،   وقبيحا في المروءة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet promises forgiveness to whoever recites Sūrat Araʾayta, provided that person pays zakāh.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  من قرأ ( سورة أرأيت )
